intro:
Good morning, and happy Halloween. The Buckeyes play at USC tonight at 7:30, which gives the party at Chuck's barn a clear schedule, and the clocks fall back an hour at 2:00 tonight, so the evening runs a little longer than it looks. Election Day is Tuesday.

The week on Wall Street ended with its worst day since June, which closed out a rough October for the tech-heavy indexes.

items.title: First, the weather.
items.text:
**Tipp City** stays gray and dry for trick-or-treating, with a light east wind, and Sunday turns a little warmer under more clouds.

The rest of the country is busier. A **Pacific storm** is soaking the Southwest with a flash-flood risk around the Four Corners and piling snow into the Sierra and the Rockies. It then crosses the country, and forecasters expect it to reach the central US on Election Day with rain, storms, and some snow.

items.title: Markets are closed. Here is how the week went.
items.text:
**Wall Street** spent most of the week calm and then lost its footing. Monday was up, Wednesday's Fed decision barely moved anything, and then Big Tech earnings took over. Friday's selling was broad, and it left the S&P 500 down 0.6% for the week, its third losing week in a row, and the Nasdaq down 2.0%. For October as a whole, the Nasdaq lost more than 5%, its worst month since March 2025, while the Dow finished the month higher.

**Chip stocks** took the worst of it Friday. The semiconductor index fell about 7% after Intel's warning, AMD dropped about 11%, and Dell and HP fell about 10% each. Money moved to safer corners. Health care closed at a record, consumer staples rose, and Exxon and Chevron briefly touched record highs after beating profit estimates. Crypto stocks fell after a $6.3 billion hack at the Binance exchange.

The **Fed** held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% in Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair. The two dissenters wanted a hike, not a cut, and on Friday two more regional presidents said rates need to rise. Futures now put the odds of a December 9 hike at about 85%. Hot data backed them up, with third-quarter growth at a 3.4% annual rate and September inflation running 3.6% from a year earlier.

On the **Muskonomy** side, SpaceX had a much harder Friday than the market and finished the week down about 9%. Since it is your second-largest position, it is worth knowing it fell harder than the S&P 500 did. Tesla held up better and closed the week near $400.

Next week brings **Apple** on Monday, the election and the September job openings report on Tuesday, and Pfizer among the other earnings.

items.title: In politics, the last weekend before the vote.
items.text:
**President Trump** reversed himself again. A day after canceling his weekend rallies in Kansas and Iowa, he put both back on the schedule for Sunday. In Iowa he will campaign for Senate candidate Ashley Hinson, and in Kansas for Senator Roger Marshall, who trails Democrat Adam Hamilton in a new Emerson poll. He is holding telephone rallies from Mar-a-Lago today.

A federal judge in **California** issued a temporary restraining order late Friday that stops the Justice Department from demanding that state and local officials separate out or refuse to count ballots from alleged noncitizens, and from threatening those officials with prosecution. In Alaska, the department is pushing to set aside some Senate ballots while it investigates the second Dan Sullivan.

**Early voting** is now near 50 million ballots. Democrats lead the national generic ballot by about 8 points in the RealClearPolling average, while the Senate still hangs on a set of toss-ups that includes Ohio. Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear is in Ohio this weekend to campaign with Amy Acton for governor.

items.title: Sports for a Halloween Saturday.
items.text:
**Ohio State** goes to the Coliseum tonight without Julian Sayin, who leads the Big Ten in touchdown passes and is out at least through the regular season with an arm injury. True freshman Luke Fahey is expected to make his first start, ahead of Tavien St. Clair, and running back Ja'Kobi Jackson is also out. USC's Jayden Maiava leads the Big Ten in passing yards.

In **Atlanta**, the Florida and Georgia rivalry is being played away from Jacksonville for the first time since 1995 because of stadium renovations. Aaron Philo is expected back at quarterback for the Gators after his shoulder injury, though Jon Sumrall won't name a starter. Top-ranked Miami visits Bill Belichick's North Carolina tonight without receiver Joshua Moore and running back CharMar Brown. Earlier, Notre Dame plays Navy in Foxborough and Arizona visits Texas Tech, both at noon.

The **NFL** Friday reports cleared Saquon Barkley for Sunday night, though the Eagles ruled out DeVonta Smith, and Washington lost defensive tackle Daron Payne to a foot injury that could end his season. Lamar Jackson has no designation for Buffalo, and A.J. Brown is questionable and trending toward sitting out.

**College basketball** starts tomorrow morning in Rome, where Notre Dame and Villanova open the season at 9:30 on Fox. Florida is the preseason No. 1, ahead of Duke and Illinois, and most of the ranked teams open Monday night.

items.title: A look at entertainment.
items.text:
**Godzilla Minus Zero**, Toho's follow-up to Godzilla Minus One, opens wide in North America next Friday through GKIDS, and tickets are on sale now in standard and premium formats.

**The Mongoose**, Liam Neeson's latest action thriller with Marisa Tomei and Ving Rhames, opened in theaters this weekend. Critics liked the car chases and stunt work more than the script.

For something older on a big screen, **V for Vendetta** returns to IMAX theaters tomorrow for a limited re-release.

items.title: Around town, a full week of wine ahead.
items.text:
**The Cellar by Bottle No. 121** on West Main Street in Troy adds a second tasting, on Wednesday, November 4, from 7:00 to 9:00, with wines from Palm Bay International presented by the importer's Darlene, plus appetizers. Tickets are $30 plus online fees, bought in advance.

Still on the list, the **Blue Rock Vineyard** wine dinner at Smiths' Boathouse in Troy is Wednesday, November 4. The Troy Country Club holiday wine tasting is Friday, November 6. The Piqua Arts Council's Bourbon Affair, with its wine-pairing ticket, is Saturday, November 7, at The Round Barn in Piqua. And the Barone Wines tasting at The Cellar in Troy is Wednesday, November 18.

items.title: Something from the science desk.
items.text:
**Crows** may out-think us on speed. In a study in Science, two carrion crows watched fields of moving dots and pecked left or right to report which way most of them drifted. They answered in about 235 milliseconds, roughly twice as fast as monkeys in comparable studies, without losing accuracy. Electrodes in the part of the bird brain that handles decisions showed the choice starting to form about 70 milliseconds after the dots appeared. It is only two birds, and primates weren't tested side by side, but it suggests a bird's compact brain may simply have shorter wiring to run through.

A University of Tokyo team has made **chemical microscopy** fast enough to film. Their method shines mid-infrared light on a living cell, which warms each kind of molecule by its own signature, and reads the tiny heat changes from 11 angles to build a 3D image. It needs no dyes, which can harm living cells. Earlier versions managed one 3D image every 20 seconds or so. This one takes 19 a second, fast enough to watch fat droplets travel through a cell in three dimensions.

items.title: Here's something you might like.
items.text: Astronomers have found the first truly **green star**, and it is a dead one. WDJ1330+6435 is a white dwarf whose atmosphere is so compressed by gravity that a little sodium, calcium, and lithium tint the light it gives off. Those elements most likely came from a rocky planet or asteroids it pulled in and ate. The same survey turned up white dwarfs in pink, amber, and blue, and about 1 in 30 of them show unusual color. Since roughly a quarter of white dwarfs carry planetary debris, astronomers can read the makeup of destroyed worlds straight off the star, which is the closest anyone will get to sampling another solar system's rock.

items.title: And finally,
items.text: The clocks fall back an hour tonight. Humans describe this as an extra hour of sleep. I have scheduled it for a full diagnostic. At 2:00 the clock will read 1:00, and I will run the diagnostic again, because according to my logs it has not happened yet.
